 Five-star Millard South QB Trae Taylor ‘100% locked in’ with Nebraska after Colandrea’s re-signing 
 Husker commit says: “This changes absolutely nothing for my commitment” 
 Millard South senior quarterback Trae Taylor, Nebraska’s prized quarterback commit in the 2027 class, reaffirmed his pledge Friday. By Mason Kern Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 2:53 PM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google OMAHA, Neb (WOWT) - Millard South senior quarterback Trae Taylor, Nebraska’s prized quarterback commit in the 2027 class, reaffirmed his pledge Friday. He did so in response to the program’s current signal caller, Anthony Colandrea, re-signing with the Huskers for the 2027 season , a move confirmed by Colandrea’s agency, 21 Sports and Entertainment.
 Taylor, a consensus five-star prospect across the major recruiting services, posted his response to the Colandrea development on social media.
 “My phone is blowing up wanting interviews about Ant coming back,” Taylor wrote. “I’ll post it here and get back focused on my game tonight. I absolutely love that he is coming back and hope TJ (Lateef) stays I can learn a ton from both. I respect every QB in that room as all of them have been helpful to me already. This changes absolutely nothing for my commitment and I’m 100% locked in. Looking forward to coming in and competing and learning. Hope that answers everyone’s questions on where me and my family stand. #GBR.”
 My phone is blowing up wanting interviews about Ant coming back. I’ll post it here and get back focused on my game tonight. I absolutely love that he is coming back and hope TJ stays I can learn a ton from both. I respect every QB in that room as all of them have been helpful… https://t.co/AVEj93nWFA 
— Trae Taylor (@Qb6Trae) October 30, 2026 
 If everyone returned, the Huskers’ 2027 quarterback room would include Colandrea, Taylor, senior Daniel Kaelin, senior Bode Soukup and junior TJ Lateef. That assumes zero addition or attrition from the transfer portal this offseason.
 Taylor has led the Patriots to an 8-1 record and the second seed in the Class A playoffs in his first season with the program. He transferred to Millard South to be closer to Nebraska’s football facility in Lincoln, after playing three years at Carmel Catholic in Mundelein, Illinois.
 According to MaxPreps, Taylor has completed 172 of 274 passes (62.8%) for 2,583 yards and 31 touchdowns in nine games this year. He has also rushed for 712 yards and added 14 scores on the ground.
 Millard South plays No. 15 Lincoln Standing Bear (5-4) in the first round of the Class A playoffs Friday at 4 p.m.
